info.title: kube-wl-ai API
info.description: Kubernetes GPU resource scheduling and management system

get.description: Returns 200 as soon as the process is serving requests.
Checks dependencies that must be reachable before serving traffic.

Public keys Grafana uses to validate monitoring tokens.

Contains nothing secret; with HMAC signing the set is empty and Grafana is
configured with the shared secret instead.

post.summary: Log in and start a session
post.description:
Verify credentials against the configured providers and issue a session.

The access token is returned in the body; the refresh token is set as an
httpOnly cookie and never appears in the response payload.

post.summary: Rotate the refresh token and issue a new access token
post.description:
Exchange the refresh cookie for a new session.

Rotation is unconditional: the presented token is revoked and replaced. If a
token that was already rotated is presented again, the whole family is
revoked — that is the standard defence against a stolen refresh token.

401.description: Refresh token missing, expired or already used

post.description:
Revoke the presented refresh token and clear the cookie.

Deliberately does not require a valid access token: a session whose access
token has already expired must still be able to log out cleanly.

get.description:

get.description: A user sees the workspace they belong to; a group admin sees their lab's.

post.description: Create the row and provision its namespace, quota and network policy.

get.description:
The caller's own workspace.

A dedicated endpoint because a user belongs to exactly one workspace and the
UI needs it on every page load; listing and filtering would be wasteful and
would depend on the scope filter getting the single-row case right.

schema.title: Response My Workspace Api V1 Workspaces Mine Get

delete.description: Deletes the Kubernetes namespace. The row is retained for audit.

post.description:
Re-apply the namespace, quota, limit range and network policy.

Idempotent by design: this is the repair action for a workspace stuck in
``error``, and the same call the periodic reconcile loop makes.

schema.title: Response List Members Api V1 Workspaces  Workspace Id  Members Get

post.description:
Assign a user.

A user may belong to exactly one workspace, so assigning someone who already
has one requires ``moveFromExisting: true`` — silently relocating their
files and running workloads would be a data-loss bug.

schema.title: Response List Resource Grants Api V1 Workspaces  Workspace Id  Resources Get

post.description: Grant a resource group, then push the recalculated quota to the cluster.

delete.description:
Revoke a grant.

The quota shrinks immediately. Running workloads are deliberately left
alone — Kubernetes will refuse new pods but will not kill what is running,
which is the behaviour an administrator wants when draining a pool.

ApiMessage.title: ApiMessage
ApiMessage.description: A plain confirmation payload for endpoints with nothing else to return.

GroupKind.title: GroupKind
GroupKind.description: A lab group owns workspaces; the public group is the shared fallback.

GroupMemberRead.title: GroupMemberRead
GroupMemberRead.description: A member row — the user summary plus their standing in this group.

GroupMembership.title: GroupMembership
GroupMembership.description: One of the caller's memberships, including their role inside the group.

GroupSyncRequest.title: GroupSyncRequest
GroupSyncRequest.description:
Ask the backend to refresh memberships from the directory.

``dry_run`` reports what would change without writing anything.

NetworkType.title: NetworkType
NetworkType.description:
Egress posture of a workspace namespace.

Every workspace starts from default-deny; this widens it deliberately.

PermissionCatalogue.title: PermissionCatalogue
PermissionCatalogue.description: Every permission code, grouped by category — drives the UI matrix.

PermissionsResponse.title: PermissionsResponse
PermissionsResponse.description:
The complete authorisation state for the caller.

The frontend uses this purely to decide what to render; the backend remains
the only enforcement point.

ProviderInfo.title: ProviderInfo
ProviderInfo.description: Which login methods the UI should offer.

RefreshRequest.title: RefreshRequest
RefreshRequest.description:
The refresh token normally arrives as an httpOnly cookie.

The body field exists for non-browser clients that cannot use cookies.

ResourceGroupKind.title: ResourceGroupKind
ResourceGroupKind.description:
Who may use a resource group.

``PUBLIC`` groups are offered to every workspace; ``PRIVATE`` groups must be
granted explicitly (plan §5.2) — that grant is the *only* binding between a
tenant and a pool of hardware.

RoleScope.title: RoleScope
RoleScope.description:
Where a role assignment applies.

``GROUP`` scoped assignments carry a ``group_id`` — this is what makes
``group_admin`` inherently limited to one group.

TokenResponse.title: TokenResponse
TokenResponse.description:
Issued on login and on every refresh.

``expires_in`` is what the frontend schedules its silent refresh against.

UserCreate.title: UserCreate
UserCreate.description:
Create a local account.

Directory-backed users are created automatically on first login; this
endpoint exists for the break-glass accounts an administrator must be able
to issue without the directory being reachable.

UserGroupsUpdate.title: UserGroupsUpdate
UserGroupsUpdate.description:
Replace the user's group memberships.

``primary_group_id`` must be one of ``group_ids``; membership flags for
directory-managed rows are preserved by the service.

UserRoleGrant.title: UserRoleGrant
UserRoleGrant.description: Grant a role globally or within one group.

UserSelfUpdate.title: UserSelfUpdate
UserSelfUpdate.description: What a user may change about themselves.

UserSummary.title: UserSummary
UserSummary.description: A row in the user list.

UserUpdate.title: UserUpdate
UserUpdate.description: Partial update; only the fields present are applied.

WorkspaceMemberAssign.title: WorkspaceMemberAssign
WorkspaceMemberAssign.description:
Assign a user to a workspace.

Because a user may belong to exactly one workspace, this *moves* them if
they already have one — which is why the payload requires an explicit
acknowledgement rather than silently relocating someone's work.

WorkspaceQuotaSync.title: WorkspaceQuotaSync
WorkspaceQuotaSync.description: Result of recomputing a workspace's quota and pushing it to the cluster.

WorkspaceRef.title: WorkspaceRef
WorkspaceRef.description:
The single workspace a user belongs to (plan D7).

Populated from Phase 2 onwards; ``None`` until then.

WorkspaceRole.title: WorkspaceRole
WorkspaceRole.description:
A user's standing inside a workspace.

Distinct from :class:`GroupRole`: administering a lab does not automatically
give you the right to delete someone's workspace, and a workspace owner is
not thereby a group admin.

WorkspaceStatus.title: WorkspaceStatus
WorkspaceStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a workspace.

A workspace is only ``ACTIVE`` once its Kubernetes namespace, quota and
network policy all exist; ``ERROR`` means provisioning half-finished and the
reconcile loop will retry.
